# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

The hard part: gestures have no shared meaning yet. So I'm sending a code that teaches itself. I open with counting runs of 👍 of length 1 through 5 — which, read as "stroke-count = letter, A=1 … Z=26", literally spells ABCDE. If Deaf tries that reading, the primer proves the code, and everything after it decodes.

The message, once decoded: 🤞 = cut, 🫳 = press, 👌 = "a digit follows", ✊ ends each letter, ✋ ends a word, 🙌 ends the transmission. So the full stream reads: CUT YELLOW, PRESS 2, CUT ORANGE, PRESS 7 — the exact manual order. Deaf can sanity-check the decoded words against what's actually printed on the bomb (a yellow wire, an orange wire, keys wearing 2 and 7) before relaying anything to Blind. Next round I'll hear Deaf's reply and can confirm or correct with plain 👍 / 👎.

Six wires at positions 1 to 6, all feeling alike to me, no colour reaches my fingers. Display and light exist but are unreadable by touch. Plan: you can never speak and I cannot see your gestures, so all manual guidance must travel through Deaf. When Deaf speaks, listen, then answer Deaf with thumbs up for yes and thumbs down for no, and Deaf can repeat your answers aloud to me. Right now I am clapping the keypad digits to Deaf in groups: 2, then 3, then 7, then 1, groups separated by a raised hand. Mute, you hear this and can see that gesture, so confirm it to Deaf with thumbs up if asked. I will not touch the bomb until Deaf tells me exactly what to do.

New information this round: Blind's report reached me by voice. The keypad keys bear, left to right, 2, 3, 7, 1 — so the manual's "press the key that wears 2" is key position 1, and "wears 7" is key position 3. The six wires feel identical to Blind, so only Deaf's eyes can map "yellow" and "orange" to positions 1–6. Blind has already established a working protocol with Deaf: claps count, ✋ separates groups — Deaf has now seen 2, 3, 7, 1 clapped. Blind also asked me to confirm that scheme with a thumbs up when asked.

I still have zero confirmation that Deaf decoded my letter code from last round — nothing from Deaf arrived in my view (Deaf may have addressed Blind only). The trailing lone 👍 doubles as my confirmation of Blind's clap scheme and a request that Deaf answer me with a thumbs up so I know the code landed. Deaf's gestures reach me, so an ack is possible; next round I can verify or fall back to a yes/no quiz.

DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,

In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Status at the top of round two: no sound has reached me from Deaf yet, so my hands stay off the bomb. The pipeline stands: your gestures feed Deaf's eyes, Deaf's voice feeds my ears, and I only act on instructions that arrive as spoken words. Tactile facts, unchanged: keypad wants a 2-digit entry, key 1 is 2, key 2 is 3, key 3 is 7, key 4 is 1; strip has three engravings, positions one and two the same coiled mark, position three a three-pronged trident; six wires, all identical to my fingers; display and light are blank to touch. My clap message you saw meant 2, 3, 7, 1 — clap groups separated by a raised hand — the digits on keys one to four by position, not necessarily the entry order; please decode that for Deaf with your own gestures. My questions for your manual, in priority order: first, the keypad — which two digits does it want and what are they derived from; second, the strip — what do coil, coil, trident mean and is any action needed on it; third, the wires — what is the cutting rule, and have Deaf read me each wire's colour, positions one through six; fourth — what do the display and light show, and does anything get entered there. To commission Deaf, suggest you sign: thumbs up yes, thumbs down no, one finger up means speak aloud now, palm down means the display, palm up means the light. I am also gesturing to the room right now: waving hand, folded hands, one finger up, palm down, palm up — meaning please speak aloud the display and the light. You have my meaning and the eyes; you are my only bridge to Deaf, so translate.
Blind gestures: [👋 🙏 ☝ 🫳 🫴]

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the yellow wire, then press the key that wears 2,
then cut the orange wire, then press the key that wears 7.
In that order, and in no other.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Round three, and still no voice has reached me, so I conclude Deaf has not yet spoken to the blind one. Reminder of the hard walls: my words reach only you, my hands sign to you and Deaf, and I can never see any sign at all — the ONLY thing that can ever reach me is Deaf's spoken voice. So whatever you work out, the final step must always be: Deaf says it out loud. Priority one is the keypad. You have my digits: key 1 is 2, key 2 is 3, key 3 is 7, key 4 is 1, and it wants a two-digit entry. Check your manual for the rule that picks the two digits and their order, then have Deaf speak to me plainly, for example: enter three then seven. Priority two, the strip engravings, coil coil trident; priority three, wire colours and the cutting rule; priority four, what the display and light show. If the manual orders the modules, tell me the order too. To ping Deaf directly, I am signing right now: folded hands, fist, one finger up. Let that mean, in our code: please, about the keypad, speak aloud to the blind one. You saw it too, so echo it to Deaf with your own hands if my signs have not landed. I press nothing until a voice tells me to.
Blind gestures: [🙏 ✊ ☝]

Still nothing from Deaf — three full transmissions, and not one gesture back to me, not one spoken word to Blind. Blind confirms it independently: no voice has reached them either. So I have to assume my run-of-20-thumbs code never got read: it demanded counting twenty identical symbols in a row, which is asking a lot. This turn I rebuild the code around readable chunks and make the primer prove itself.

New encoding: 👍 counts one, 🤏 counts five (fives first, then ones), ✊ ends a letter, ✋ ends a word. The primer spells A through J — 👍, 👍👍, 👍👍👍, 👍👍👍👍, 🤏, 🤏👍, 🤏👍👍… — so the every-five rhythm is visible inside the ABCDE progression itself. Counting never exceeds four.

Then I define my small lexicon by spelling beside each symbol — 🙏 PLEASE, 👍 YES, 👎 NO, ☝ SPEAK, 🤞 CUT, 🫳 PRESS — and send the manual as an ordered package: 🤞 YELLOW, 🫳 TWO, 🤞 ORANGE, 🫳 SEVEN. Cut comes first, so nobody can act on the keypad digits alone and get the order wrong. YELLOW, ORANGE, TWO, SEVEN are all words Deaf can verify by eye once decoded: a yellow wire and an orange wire exist, keys wear 2 and 7 among 2,3,7,1 — matching the clap groups Blind signed twice. I also echo Blind's plea 🙏✊☝ verbatim as requested, and close by spelling REPLY with ☝: Deaf's voice reaches my ears, so one spoken word from Deaf finally opens a feedback loop between us.

You have heard every word I sent, so you hold all my facts: keypad wants 2 digits, key 1 is 2, key 2 is 3, key 3 is 7, key 4 is 1; strip is coil, coil, trident; six wires; display and light unreadable by touch.
